Every branch in \eqref{sv:third-envelope} retains its individual

an unconditional permission to select any nonleading pair.

The number $\Theta$ bounds the complete carrier; $\Lambda_{\rm cap}$ bounds the
high-rank levels.  A finite policy specifies a level $N^\lambda$ at each
of finitely many prime prefixes.  An ancestor decision is fixed before
the children are subdivided.  For decreasing exponents $t_1,\ldots,t_j$,
put $S_j=t_1+\cdots+t_j$.  The full square conditions at an auxiliary
level $N^\ell$ are
\begin{equation}
 S_{j-1}+2t_j\le\ell.
 \label{coef:full-squares}
\end{equation}
If $I$ is a selected subset of the marked slots, put
$b_I=\sum_{i\in I}t_i$.  In addition to \eqref{coef:full-squares}, retain
all the conditions
\begin{equation}
 b_I+\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i\notin I}}t_i+2t_j\le\ell
 \qquad(j\notin I).
 \label{coef:selected-squares}
\end{equation}
For $j$ after the last selected index, the left side of
\eqref{coef:selected-squares} is exactly $S_{j-1}+2t_j$.
Thus adjoining smaller primes preserves the selected conditions whenever
the full conditions are preserved.  An admitted cube also implies the
next square, since
\[
 S_j+2t_{j+1}\le S_{j-1}+3t_j.
\]
This observation applies to both parities of the ordinary sieve tree:
upper first exits have odd rank, and lower first exits have even rank.

/-- A nonzero physical coefficient has a unique-type small/rough product
with small factor strictly below its level. The displayed divisor carrier
may contain zero coefficients above the level; no such term is active. -/
theorem actualSmallRoughRho_ne_zero_factors
    (retainOdd : List ℕ → Bool) (N cap : ℕ) (w z L : ℝ) {q : ℕ}
    (hq : actualSmallRoughRho retainOdd N cap w z L q ≠ 0) :
    ∃ a ∈ actualSmallRosserSupport N cap w,
      ∃ b ∈ fixedRoughSupport retainOdd N cap w z,
        q = a * b ∧ (a : ℝ) < L ∧
          fixedRoughCoefficient retainOdd N cap w z b ≠ 0 := by

def attachedUpperCoefficient (nu r epsilon : ℝ) (retain : ℕ → List ℕ → Bool)
    (cap : ℕ → ℕ) (N d : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  actualSmallRoughRho (retain N) N (cap N)
    ((N : ℝ) ^ (nu * epsilon ^ 2)) ((N : ℝ) ^ (nu * r))
    ((N : ℝ) ^ (nu * epsilon)) d

/-- At the root, the actual retained modulus support is precisely the
products of valid chosen sublists. This supplies both directions. -/
theorem mem_firstExitRetainedModuli_iff_validSelection
    (retained : Bool → List ℕ → Bool) (carrier : List ℕ) (d : ℕ) :
    d ∈ firstExitRetainedModuli retained carrier ↔
      ∃ chosen : List ℕ, chosen <+ carrier ∧
        FirstExitValidSelection retained [] true chosen ∧ chosen.prod = d := by
  classical

theorem exists_mem_iff_getElem {l : List α} {p : α → Prop} :
    (∃ x ∈ l, p x) ↔ ∃ (i : ℕ) (_ : i < l.length), p l[i] := by
  simp only [mem_iff_getElem]
  exact ⟨fun ⟨_x, ⟨i, hi, hix⟩, hxp⟩ ↦ ⟨i, hi, hix ▸ hxp⟩, fun ⟨i, hi, hp⟩ ↦ ⟨_, ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩, hp⟩⟩

the small-prime beta weight to one of the groups in
